question: During an evaluation of a new diagnostic imaging modality for detecting salivary gland tumors, 90 patients tested positive out of the 100 patients who tested positive with the gold standard test. A total of 80 individuals tested negative with the new test out of the 100 individuals who tested negative with the gold standard test. What is the positive likelihood ratio for this test?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: True positive (TP) = 90 False negative (FN) = 10 True negative (TN) = 80 False positive (FP) = 20 -> Calculate positive likelihood ratio (PLR) = (TP / (FP) = 90 / 20 = 4.5 -> 90%
enhanced_information: The positive likelihood ratio for the test is 4.5, calculated as 90/20. This indicates that the test is 4.5 times more likely to be positive in patients with the condition compared to those without the condition.
analysis: The positive likelihood ratio (LR+) is calculated as the ratio of true positive rate to false positive rate. In this case, LR+ = True Positive Rate / False Positive Rate = 90/20 = 4.5. This indicates that the test is 4.5 times more likely to be positive in patients with the condition compared to those without the condition.
